## What We Did

Reviewed logistic regression and learned about ROC curves.

## Key Concepts

#### Specificity vs Sensitivity Review:

- Sensitivity is about true positives, specificity is about true negatives 
- If we lower the cutoff threshold (for determining 0 vs 1 designation), sensitivity will go up
  - High sensitivity is basically a "better safe than sorry" approach to an issue
  - Sensitivity is also the same as the true positive rate
- If we raise the cutoff threshold, specificity will go up
  - Specificity is NOT the same as the false positive rate

"Accuracy is a farce" because it does not consider what types of errors occurred 

- A model can have high accuracy (i.e. lowest number of errors), but not be the "best" model because it has a high number of false negatives (which in some contexts is very bad)


#### ROC (Receiving Operator Characteristic) Curves

- Developed from analysis of radar accuracy during WWII
- Graph of false positive rate vs true positive rate
- Used to judge how good a model is 
  - Want to maximize the area under the curve
  - If an ROC looks like a straight line, then the model is no better than a coin-flip (an area of 0.5)
- If TPR = 1 and FPR = 0, then the model has accurately predicted all 1s and has made no errors (unattainable perfection)
  - The point in the curve that is closest to (0,1) is the most (numerically) equal trade-off between FPR and TPR
  - A result too close to perfection might signal over-fitting
- If TPR = 0 and FPR = 0, then the model has flagged all observations as 0
- If the TPR = 1 and FPR = 1, then the model has flagged all observations as 1
